rules.title: let-else else-block must diverge
rules.statement: In `let PAT = EXPR else { BLOCK };` the else BLOCK must unconditionally diverge (end in return / break / continue / panic / `loop {}`); a non-diverging else-block is a compile error.

rules.title: let-else pattern bindings escape to the enclosing scope
rules.statement: Bindings introduced by the let-else pattern are defined in the enclosing (outer) scope and remain visible after the statement; the else-block is lowered in a separate nested scope. Each binding takes its type from the matched pattern position. Bindings named `_` are not introduced.

rules.title: Refutable inner-literal tests preserved in let-else
rules.statement: A let-else pattern with refutable inner sub-patterns (e.g. `let Some(1) = e else`) tests the inner literal in addition to the variant discriminant; these inner-value guards are evaluated AFTER the bindings are bound, not dropped.

rules.title: or-pattern alternatives in let-else bind identical names/types
rules.statement: In an or-pattern let-else (`let A(x) | B(x) = v else …`) all alternatives must bind the same names with the same types; bindings are taken from the first alternative.

rules.title: Statement-position fn desugars to a let-bound closure
rules.statement: A function item at statement position `fn inner(params) [-> T] { body }` is lowered as an immutable local binding `let inner = |params| -> T { body }`; the binding's type is the closure's inferred type.

rules.title: Top-level `_` annotation defers to RHS type
rules.statement: A top-level placeholder annotation `let x: _ = rhs` drops the annotation entirely and adopts the RHS type. A nested `_` inside a composite annotation (`Vec<_>`) is a hole filled from the RHS during inference rather than dropped.

rules.title: let annotation supplies a type hint to RHS inference
rules.statement: A non-hole let annotation hints RHS literal/inference: enum/struct annotations with type-args, fn-ptr/closure annotations (so untyped closure params infer), array/slice element types (incl. through `&[T]`/`&mut [T]`), and tuple element types (so untyped int literals widen to the annotated element type instead of defaulting).

rules.title: let-init borrow of an rvalue extends the temporary
rules.statement: `let p = &<rvalue>` / `let p = &mut <rvalue>` (rvalue = scalar literal or value-producing call/struct/tuple literal) extends the temporary's lifetime to the enclosing scope: a hidden named temporary holds the value and is dropped at scope end, and the binding is rewritten to borrow that named temporary. A void/Never/error-typed rvalue keeps the degenerate inline spill (nothing to drop).

rules.title: `let ref y = x` is sugar for `let y = &x`
rules.statement: A `ref` binding `let ref y = x` (or `let ref y: T = x`) lowers to taking the address of the RHS, giving `y` type `&T`.

rules.title: let-binding a deref of a Box moves the content out
rules.statement: `let s = *b` where `b: Box<T>` and `T` is a move type moves the boxed value out (consuming `b`) and frees the block without dropping the content (Rust's built-in `*b` move). Copy-T Box and non-Box derefs use the normal copy/deref path.

rules.title: Cannot move a move-typed value out of a reference deref (E0507)
rules.statement: `let s = *r` that would move a move-typed value out of a `&`/`&mut` deref of a reference variable is rejected (E0507); copy-typed values copy out fine.

rules.title: let without initializer declares an uninitialised binding
rules.statement: `let v: T;` / `let mut v: T;` (annotation, no value) declares the binding with the annotated type and no value; the binding is recorded as declared-uninitialised so a later assignment registers the value without a drop-before-replace, and the variable must be assigned before use. `let` without value and without annotation is an error.

rules.title: Type-ascription let reborrows &mut RHS
rules.statement: A type-ascribed let `let _: T = rhs` is a coercion site: when rhs is `&mut U` and the annotation is a reference/pointer kind (`&mut`, `&`, `*`), the RHS is implicitly reborrowed, so the original `&mut` is restored after the binding's last use (NLL).

rules.title: Implicit coercions at let-init when RHS type differs from annotation
rules.statement: When the RHS type is not directly compatible with the annotation, the binding applies, in order: CoerceUnsized for smart-pointer structs (`Rc<A>` → `Rc<dyn Tr>`); `&mut [T;N]` → `&mut [T]` array-ref-to-slice decay; non-capturing closure literal → `fn(..)->T`. If none apply (and not impl-Trait / not ExprBlob) a type-mismatch error is reported.

rules.title: impl Trait let annotation adopts the concrete RHS type
rules.statement: When the annotation is `impl Trait`, the binding's type is the concrete RHS type (so inherent/method calls resolve), rather than the abstract impl-Trait type.

rules.title: Implicit safe integer widening at let-init
rules.statement: At a let-init coercion site, a concrete (non-IntLit, non-enum) integer RHS whose type can safely widen to the annotated integer type is implicitly widened (e.g. u32→i64, i32→i64, u8→u32) without an explicit `as`.
rules.divergence: Rust requires an explicit `as` cast for any integer width change; Logos performs implicit safe widening.

rules.title: Numeric literal RHS retyped to float annotation
rules.statement: A FloatLit RHS is retyped to an `f32`/`f64` annotation; an IntLit RHS under a float annotation becomes a float literal (simple literal) or an `as`-cast to float (non-literal IntLit expression).

rules.title: Integer literal must fit the annotated type
rules.statement: An integer literal RHS (scalar, or per-element of an array/tuple literal, recursively into nested array/tuple literals) whose value does not fit in the annotated (element) integer type is a compile error.

rules.title: Unannotated integer literal binding defaults to i32 (i64 on overflow)
rules.statement: An unannotated let whose RHS is an integer literal binds at type i32, upgraded to i64 when the literal value falls outside the i32 range.
rules.divergence: Rust defaults unconstrained integer literals to i32 but never silently widens to i64 on overflow (it is a compile error); Logos auto-upgrades to i64.

rules.title: Unannotated float literal binding defaults to f64
rules.statement: An unannotated let whose RHS is a float literal binds at type f64.

rules.title: let of a move-typed place marks the source moved
rules.statement: If the RHS of a let is a place (variable reference or struct-field-read chain) of a move type, the source is marked moved (recording dotted paths so per-field auto-drop on the source struct is suppressed).

rules.title: A closure-RHS let owns its captures' drop slots
rules.statement: A let whose RHS is a closure literal owns the drop slots of that closure's (un-skipped) captures; they are dropped together with the binding, in capture order.

rules.title: Owning Box<dyn Trait> binding drops only when ownership is transferred
rules.statement: An `let x: Box<dyn Trait>` binding (which collapses to a bare owning TraitObject) is marked for drop (drop_in_place + free) only when the RHS genuinely transfers ownership — a `box_new(..) as Box<dyn>` cast or a value-returning constructor call. Reads of a handle copy out of a container (deref / index / method-call) are excluded to avoid double-free.
